gen-gf-tektur-gf-prompt: Tektur draws wire-thin letters with outsized lowercase and generous openings on every curve, all in one plotter-pen line. And Prompt, a sans-serif, answers with oversized small letters and open apertures that make plain reading easy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-pt-sans-caption: Expressive and a bit strange, Tektur holds a single unbroken line from terminal to junction, with oversized lowercase. PT Sans Caption brings big-bodied letters and bowls that stay inviting, which makes the strongest single quality here the friendly, open texture of the text.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-puritan: Tektur looks like outlines drawn in one width, with wide-open curve endings. Puritan follows with rounded forms and oversized e and a counters, so its plain sans text feels soft and approachable beside that wiry heading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-questrial: Tektur turns out pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase that get noticed right away, which is its best trick. Questrial does the opposite job, a plain sans with flat, stencil-cut single-weight letters and a tall band of lowercase that keeps text tidy.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-radio-canada: Tall, full c, s and z shapes make Radio Canada read with a steady, pressure-free line and clear curve openings. Tektur is the one that grabs attention with its pipe-cleaner strokes, and Radio Canada is the one that carries the words quietly afterward.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-radio-canada-big: Contemporary and unfussy, Tektur still has expressive pipe-cleaner strokes. Radio Canada Big gives the pair its strongest quality, a monoline sans with a tall x-height and terminals finishing well clear of the stem.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-readex-pro: Neutral in temperament, Readex Pro keeps its text steady under Tektur's wiry headings. Over a long stretch, Readex Pro stays unvarying in weight, with broad gaps at the terminals and a tiny gap between lowercase and caps.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-roboto: Wire-like and wide-mouthed, Tektur has tubular letterforms with outsized lowercase. Roboto sits below as a plain sans with generous round letters, so body text at a modest size lets the heading carry the attitude.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-ruda: Pipe-cleaner strokes and outsized lowercase make Tektur look like bent wire. Ruda, a sans-serif with a wire-like monoline of its own, adds a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds, so the two feel related but not identical.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-saira: Expressive from its first word, Tektur gives every stem, bowl and tail a rope-like consistency. Saira, a plain sans, brings see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching toward the top line, which keeps the text clean beneath it.
